feedback.observed: The generic frontend-design skill kept being activated even after project-specific motion research had been completed and preserved, adding context without improving the direction.
feedback.expected: Use the preserved green-movement shot contract and measured 700px frames as the motion authority; return to external or generic design guidance only when the project evidence has a named gap.
feedback.evidence: The Obsidian study now contains sourced staging, continuity, typography, timing, rejection, and Gate rules specific to this SVG, while the generic skill contributed no uncovered job in the latest pass.
feedback.reproduction: Inspect the active capability routing and the next motion candidate; frontend-design must not activate, and each motion decision must map to the project shot contract or a measured source defect.

feedback.observed: Several successive turnover fixes improved empty time, endpoint distance, footprint clearance, and bridge speed, but the user still had to identify that the continuous carrier path communicated the wrong identity story.
feedback.expected: For an identity or continuity complaint, inspect the actor lifecycle and adjacent rendered frames before optimizing another coordinate metric; test what story the uninterrupted trajectory communicates.
feedback.evidence: V21, v25, and v26 passed their numeric turnover checks, yet the v26 source still reused one field-slot actor and moved the UFO directly from the outgoing pickup to the incoming drop. The first diagnosis that traced both facts produced the bounded service-cut correction.
feedback.reproduction: For the next actor-identity motion report, require a source lifecycle trace plus pickup-to-next-action frame sequence before proposing a spatial or timing change.

feedback.observed: The first UFO still slid in from outside, opening sheep 2 through 4 used visible cross-field carrier travel, and the 0.104-second replacement flight still exposed intermediate UFO positions. This made deployment feel like sheep entering from offscreen instead of appearing at their assigned cells.
feedback.expected: Use one point-flash grammar for initial deployment and replacement: no visible intermediate UFO body, no offstage first entry, and sheep revealed only at exact destination cells after the arrival flash.
feedback.evidence: Fresh v29 frames showed the first entry descending from above, opening UFO positions interpolating across the field, and five visible carrier positions during the first turnover. The v30 candidate holds the hidden first UFO at its drop, hides deployments 2 through 6 for the final 0.052 playback seconds before each destination, hides turnover motion for 0.104 seconds, and retains exact-drop sheep transforms.
feedback.reproduction: Inspect adjacent 700px frames around the first arrival, opening deployments 2 through 4, and first, maximum-distance, and final turnovers; reject any offstage slide, visible intermediate UFO or sheep body, missing destination light, or off-drop sheep reveal.

proposals.change_target: first UFO appearance, opening inter-drop continuity, turnover visibility, destination light, deterministic SVG checks, README behavior description, and durable motion guardrails
proposals.cause: The source treated fast travel as a visibly interpolated carrier path and still initialized the first UFO above the field. Exact sheep anchors could not prevent the carrier motion from communicating an offscreen delivery.
proposals.candidate_change: Initialize the UFO invisibly at the exact first drop, reveal it through the existing destination light, hold at each completed deployment stop until a hidden 0.052-second coordinate jump, and hide every turnover UFO through its existing 0.104-second exchange window. Keep sheep spawn, landing, and ready transforms fixed at exact destinations.
proposals.discovery_evidence: Adjacent v29 frames reproduced the offstage first descent and intermediate UFO body during opening and turnover travel. Adjacent v30 frames show an empty field before the first exact-drop flash, no UFO body during deployments 2 through 6 or turnover coordinate changes, and destination-only UFO and sheep reveals.
proposals.reproduction: Run npm run visual:fixture and npm run check; inspect fresh 700px forced-theme adjacent first-entry, opening 2 through 6, first/later/final turnover, reduced-motion, roster, finale, and terminal frames.
proposals.primary_metric: Zero visible intermediate UFO or sheep frames during first entry, all five opening inter-drop jumps, and all 22 turnover jumps, with one existing-light destination flash and exact-drop sheep reveal for every deployment.
proposals.prediction: One hidden point-flash grammar across deployment and turnover will eliminate the offscreen-slide impression more reliably than further reducing visible travel duration, without adding assets or effects.
proposals.falsification_condition: Reject if the first UFO slides from outside, any opening or turnover jump exposes an intermediate body, a destination flash or exact-drop sheep reveal is missing, an incoming sheep appears before its panel handoff, any accepted causal or layout check regresses, runtime exceeds 50 seconds, or npm run check fails.
proposals.regression_check: npm run check plus a fresh exact-time 700px Gate across first entry, opening drops, multiple turnovers, themes, reduced motion, 10/28/62 rosters, finale, and terminal state.
proposals.transfer_check: Not applicable; this is a project-scoped motion correction.
